# Inspector Nextgen E2E — Agent Guide

> **Audience:** humans and LLM agents writing or debugging tests in `rasa/core/channels/inspector-nextgen/e2e/`.
> Read this first. Worked examples: [docs/authoring-tests.md](docs/authoring-tests.md). Setup and env: [README.md](README.md).

## Stack requirements

From repo root before `yarn e2e`: `make install`, `source .venv/bin/activate` (same as [inspector-e2e-tests action](../../../../../.github/actions/inspector-e2e-tests/action.yml)).

Load `e2e/.env` (see [README.md](README.md#environment)):

- **`DEEPGRAM_API_KEY`**, **`OPENAI_API_KEY`**, **`RASA_PRO_LICENSE`** — required (checked by `scripts/e2e-setup.sh`)

**Unified setup** — `scripts/e2e-setup.sh` is the single supervisor for local and CI: mock MCP on `:8765` → `rasa train` in `agents/calm/` → `rasa inspect` on `:5005` → block on background jobs. `yarn e2e` and CI both wrap it with `start-server-and-test` waiting on `http://localhost:5005`. In CI, `BROWSER=echo` is set when `CI=true`.

**Agents** — two run side by side under `e2e/agents/`: `agents/calm/` (v1 finance CALM, `assistant_id: inspector-e2e`) on **:5005** and `agents/mantle/` (pinned copy of `examples/mantle-banking`, a hybrid Mantle skill bot) on **:5006**. The setup script trains and serves both; after YAML changes rerun `yarn e2e` / `yarn e2e:setup` (on-disk YAML ≠ packaged `models/*.tar.gz`). One Playwright project (`chromium`) runs everything on `BASE_URL`; `tests/mantle/` opt into :5006 with `test.use({ baseURL: MANTLE_BASE_URL })` and are runnable on their own via `yarn e2e:only:mantle`. Skill-mode UI (skill document, memory-grouped-by-skill, provenance badges) is testable **only** against the mantle agent — `skill_state` is Mantle-only. Skill routing is LLM-driven, so specs pin catalog display names at the welcome turn and at end-of-turn via `activateSkillMode` (e.g. Session Start, Card Disambiguation). Do not assert an intermediate `call:` skill mid-turn.

**Inspector for Playwright** — `rasa inspect --port 5005` (Socket.IO at `/inspector.io`, not REST). `POST /webhooks/rest/webhook` on inspect → 404.

Magic utterances: [agents/calm/docs/E2E_TRIGGERS.md](agents/calm/docs/E2E_TRIGGERS.md) (also in welcome/help).

## Running tests

| Command | When |
| --- | --- |
| `yarn e2e` | Full path via SST: `e2e-setup.sh` (MCP + train + inspect) → Playwright |
| `yarn e2e:setup` | Foreground `e2e-setup.sh`; run `yarn e2e:only` in another terminal |
| `yarn e2e:only` | Mock MCP + inspect already up |
| `yarn e2e:only tests/<file>.test.ts` | Develop/debug one file |
| `yarn e2e:only tests/<file>.test.ts -g "test name"` | Single case |
| `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` | Types/barrel exports before Playwright |

Also: `yarn e2e:watch` (headed), `yarn e2e:debug`, `yarn e2e:repeat` (flakes).

`yarn e2e:only` does **not** start mock MCP or inspect.

## Debugging

Use when Playwright fails, the bot misbehaves outside the UI, or you need locators before authoring.

**Health checks** (both should return `200`):

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:5005/
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8765/health
```

Run only **one** `rasa inspect` on `:5005`. Extra inspect processes or overlapping `yarn e2e:only` runs cause `net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` and false batch failures.

**Two ways to talk to the bot:**

| Mode | Command | Client |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inspector UI | `cd agents/calm && rasa inspect --port 5005` | Socket.IO (`user_message` + `session_id`) — Playwright default |
| REST smoke | `rasa run --connector rest --port <free-port> --model models/*.tar.gz` | `POST /webhooks/rest/webhook` — use a **fresh `sender` per conversation** |

REST smoke example (from `agents/calm/` after train):

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:5055/webhooks/rest/webhook" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"sender":"smoke-'"$(date +%s)"'","message":"say hello"}'
```

**Recommended order**

1. Confirm mock MCP + inspect health.
2. REST-smoke one magic utterance with a fresh `sender` (agent contract).
3. `yarn e2e:only tests/<file>.test.ts`, then `-g "exact title"` if needed.
4. Post-mortem — **trace CLI before** GUI `yarn report` / `show-trace`:

   **`test-results/<test>/` on failure has:** assertion error (terminal too), screenshot, `error-context.md` (ARIA snapshot at failure — good for locators; **not** a substitute for the action timeline), and `trace.zip` (`trace: retain-on-failure`; passing tests do not write a zip).

   **Trace CLI** (local `@playwright/test` 1.60.0 — run from `e2e/`):

   ```bash
   npx playwright trace open test-results/<test>/trace.zip
   npx playwright trace actions --errors-only
   npx playwright trace action <action-id>
   npx playwright trace console --errors-only
   npx playwright trace snapshot <action-id>
   npx playwright trace close
   ```

   **Trace CLI adds:** numbered action timeline (durations, locator strings), `--errors-only`, `action <id>` with source file:line, and `console` / `requests` when network or browser logs matter. **Often enough without it:** failure on the first assertion with little UI setup (terminal + `error-context.md`). **`trace snapshot`:** may need `npx playwright install` if the CLI browser revision does not match installed browsers.

   **GUI fallback:** `yarn report` or `yarn playwright show-trace test-results/.../trace.zip`.

5. **`playwright-cli`** against a live inspect session for locator fixes — [`.claude/skills/playwright-cli/SKILL.md`](.claude/skills/playwright-cli/SKILL.md).
6. After agent/domain edits: retrain, restart inspect, re-run Playwright.

**Session isolation:** Use a fresh `sender` / Socket.IO `session_id` for magic-utterance and inspector-diagnostic checks. Do not chain them after mid-flow finance setup (e.g. “Add @tester”) in the same session. Call `restartConversation` (or new REST sender) before each diagnostic test.

**Channel-scoped NLG:** Responses with only `channel: browser_audio` break text chat (Playwright, REST) with `No response variation selected`. Add default `- text:` variants (or remove the channel filter), then retrain.

**Diagnostic flows:** Magic utterances (`inspector test …`, Context7, DeepWiki) use LLM + mock MCP. Assert **log event labels**, details panels, error dots, timeline status — **not** bot reply text. Multi-turn collects may need fixed follow-ups (1–3 turns).

## Test shape

Tests orchestrate **flows** and **inline steps** — not raw Playwright locators outside triads. Thin spec example: [docs/authoring-tests.md § Writing a simple shell test](docs/authoring-tests.md#writing-a-simple-shell-test).

- Setup via **fixtures**; prefer `test.use({ inspectorOptions: ... })` over `test.beforeEach` for fixture-shaped setup.
- **Reusable multi-step journeys** in **flows**; **single-use or spec-local checks** inline in `*.test.ts` via `ui.*` + `test.step`.
- Atomic UI in **triads** under `actions/ui/`.
- Selectors only inside `getLocators(...)` per UI module.
- Prefer **flow calls** for shared journeys; when a spec calls `ui.*` **actions** or **assertions** directly, wrap each logical group in **`test.step`** (see [§ `test.step` in specs](#teststep-in-specs)).

### When to use flows vs inline

| Put it in a **flow** | Keep it **inline in the spec** |
| --- | --- |
| Used in **2+ tests** (same or different files) | Used in **one test only** |
| Multi-step journey composed by specs (`open → assert → close`) | One or two `test.step` blocks tied to that spec's scenario |
| Expensive setup shared across cases (diagnostic trigger, memory flow) | Viewport resize, route intercept, or other test-only Playwright setup |
| Building blocks reused within a file (e.g. `downloads.*`, `chat.sendMessage*`) | Cheap assertion on state already established in the same test |

Do **not** add a flow export for a helper used once — inline it (see `tests/all-view.test.ts`, `tests/canvas-controls.test.ts`, `tests/voice.test.ts`). Exception: a long single-test journey (~30+ lines) may stay in a flow when it reads cleaner (`richMessages.assertInspectorMemorySlotsVisible`).

Reference specs mixing both styles: `tests/all-view.test.ts`, `tests/memory.test.ts`, `tests/conversation-history.test.ts`.

### Grouping related tests

E2E tests are expensive — each case pays for a fresh page (and often LLM or diagnostic triggers). Specs do **not** need to be one assertion per `test()`. Group cases that share setup or form one user journey; keep **actions/assertions** atomic inside flows and triads.

**Combine when:**

- Test B repeats all of test A's setup, then adds the next step (e.g. trigger events → open details panel; open panel → close and assert restored).
- Steps are sequential in a single journey (open inspect → close inspect; fit canvas → zoom in/out → reset to 100%).
- Assertions are cheap clicks on the **same session state** (flow started + flow completed details; close button + re-click to deselect).
- A longer test already covers a shorter sibling — delete the redundant case instead of keeping both.

**Keep separate when:**

- Cases need **different conversation states** or mid-flow setup (balance check vs welcome-only session).
- Cases use **different expensive triggers** (agent success vs custom-tool success; Context7 vs DeepWiki).
- Cases cover **unrelated failure modes** (flows load error vs empty-flow placeholder).
- Isolation helps debugging parallel input paths (Enter vs Send button) — only when the split is cheap.

Use **`test.step` inside flows** so grouped tests still show granular steps in traces and reports. When two flow helpers each repeat the same expensive setup (e.g. two balance-check sends), add a **combined flow** rather than calling both helpers back-to-back.

Examples: [docs/authoring-tests.md § Grouping related tests](docs/authoring-tests.md#grouping-related-tests). Reference specs: `tests/all-view.test.ts`, `tests/home.test.ts`, `tests/agent-events.test.ts`, `tests/canvas-controls.test.ts`.

### `test.step` in specs

Use `test.step` so traces and reports show named steps for every user-visible action and assertion.

| Call site | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `flows.*` at top level | OK — flows already wrap their steps |
| `ui.*.actions(...)` or `ui.*.assertions(...)` in `*.test.ts` | **Required** — wrap in `await test.step("…", async () => { … })` |
| Raw `expect(...)` or Playwright calls in `*.test.ts` | **Required** — same wrapping |

Step titles describe the outcome (`"Switch to Memory view"`, `"Assert bot message count is 2"`). Group related action + assertion in one step when they form a single check. Reused sequences belong in a **flow**, not copied steps. Sync-only steps may use a non-`async` callback: `await test.step("…", () => { expect(...) })`.

Worked example: [docs/authoring-tests.md § Direct UI in specs](docs/authoring-tests.md#direct-ui-in-specs). Reference specs: `tests/memory.test.ts`, `tests/conversation-history.test.ts`.

### Waits and assertions

LLM- and network-driven flakiness is almost always a **synchronisation** bug, not real non-determinism. Fix it at the wait, then assert exact values — never weaken an assertion to "some value" to make it pass.

- **Wait on a completion signal, not a proxy.** Gate the next step on a definitive "done" event (`conversationLog.completeTurn` → *Agent turn ended*), never on a side-effect that races the rest of the turn — a bot-message count, one slot write. The mechanics and the mid-turn-remount failure this prevents are in **Pitfalls**.
- **After synchronising, assert the exact expected value.** Pin the settled state (e.g. `activeSkillNameIs("Card Disambiguation")`), not a regex for "any value". A weakened assertion passes real regressions through — reach for it only when the value is genuinely non-deterministic after the turn settles.
- **`expect.poll` for counts and computed values.** `expect.poll(() => locator.count()).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(n)` and `expect.poll(() => readText()).toBe(expected)` retry the *derived* value; prefer them to `.nth(n-1).toBeVisible()` or reading text once.
- **One long, named timeout for async waits; the short default for UI checks.** Async/LLM waits take the shared `LLM_TIMEOUT` (`@e2e/config`); synchronous render checks keep the suite default so a genuine UI bug fails fast instead of hanging out the whole LLM budget.

## Layers

| Layer | Location | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `getLocators` | `actions/ui/<feature>.actions.ts` | Locator map |
| `actions` | same file | One interaction each |
| `assertions` | same file | One visible outcome each |
| `flows` | `flows/<feature>.flow.ts` | Journeys with `test.step(...)` |
| `fixtures` | `fixtures/<concern>-fixture.ts` | Shared setup |
| `*.test.ts` | `tests/` | Orchestrate flows; wrap direct `ui.*` calls in `test.step(...)` |

Rules: no standalone click helpers outside triads; every `expect(...)` has a failure message; assertions do not click/type; actions may `expect` only to confirm that interaction completed.

## Fixtures

In `*.test.ts` only: `import { test, expect } from "@e2e/fixtures"`.

`inspectorOptions`:

- `open` — open inspector page (default `true`)
- `inspectMode` — switch to Inspect after open, then wait for the welcome turn to end
- `query` — inspect URL query (`?token=None` or `token=None`)
- `viewport` — `{ width, height }` after navigation (suite default is `1600×900` in `playwright.config.ts`; override to shrink, e.g. `{ width: 1240, height: 768 }`)

Do not encode finance-demo conversation states in fixtures unless that becomes a suite-wide pattern.

## Imports

- `@e2e/config` → `config.ts` (`BASE_URL`, `MANTLE_BASE_URL`, `LLM_TIMEOUT`)
- `@e2e/ui-actions` → `actions/ui`
- `@e2e/flows` → `flows`
- `@e2e/fixtures` → `test` / `expect`

Style: `import * as ui from "@e2e/ui-actions"`; `import * as flows from "@e2e/flows"`.

In `flows/**`: `import { test } from "@playwright/test"` for `test.step` only — not `@e2e/fixtures`.

## Shared UI surfaces

Reuse before adding modules:

- `inspectorShell` — nav, view toggle, restart, send, readiness
- `conversationLog` — messages and events (`assistant-chat`)
- `inspectorCanvas` — flow canvas, nodes, active flow
- `eventDetails`, `viewMenu`, `historyTimeline`, `memoryPanel`, `downloads`, `voiceControls`, `modal`
- `skillSection` — Mantle skill document (prose, ordered blocks, available tools); used by `tests/mantle/` only. The skill-mode memory pane lives in `memoryPanel` alongside the v1 one — both render inside `memory-panel`.

## Flow namespaces

Import via `@e2e/flows` (export from `flows/index.ts`):

| Namespace | File | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `flows.shell` | `shell.flow.ts` | Landing, inspect toggle, restart |
| `flows.chat` | `chat.flow.ts` | Send message, event details panels |
| `flows.inspectPanel` | `inspect-panel.flow.ts` | Collected slot click |
| `flows.downloads` | `downloads.flow.ts` | Download popover |
| `flows.agent` | `agent.flow.ts` | Sub-agent diagnostic utterances |
| `flows.mcp` | `mcp.flow.ts` | MCP / Context7 / DeepWiki events |
| `flows.error` | `error.flow.ts` | Action/tool/MCP failures |
| `flows.flowLifecycle` | `flow-lifecycle.flow.ts` | Competing sub-agent flows |
| `flows.history` | `history.flow.ts` | Timeline, mid-flow Active status |
| `flows.allView` | `all-view.flow.ts` | Large-viewport All layout journeys |
| `flows.richMessages` | `rich-messages.flow.ts` | Inspector memory/buttons diagnostic flow |
| `flows.mantle` | `mantle.flow.ts` | Activate skill mode on the Mantle agent (`tests/mantle/` only) |

Canvas controls, highlighting, states, voice, and responsive viewport checks live **inline in specs** (`tests/canvas-*.test.ts`, `tests/voice.test.ts`, `tests/responsive.test.ts`) — not in flow files.

Flow files import only `@e2e/ui-actions` and `@playwright/test` — **not** other flow files; specs compose namespaces.

`restartConversation` clears **user** messages only; bot messages may remain.

## Selectors

Prefer: `getByRole` / `getByLabel` → `getByTestId` → stable text/placeholder → CSS last resort. No XPath.

Anchor on a single purpose-built `data-testid`. If the product has none for what you need to count or scope, **add one** rather than reaching for a prefix/attribute match (`[data-testid^="slot-"]`) or borrowing a parent container's id — both silently re-match or detach when unrelated markup shifts. A dedicated `memory-entry` / `memory-source` testid beats counting `slot-*` prefixes.

## Finance demo

Tests use the **inspector-e2e** agent (finance flows + inspector diagnostics). Keep stable contracts explicit; do not strengthen assertions without verifying locally. Triggers: [E2E_TRIGGERS.md](agents/calm/docs/E2E_TRIGGERS.md).

## Do not

- `import { test } from "@playwright/test"` in `*.test.ts`
- deep imports `@e2e/ui-actions/*` or `@e2e/flows/*`
- `page.waitForTimeout`, `test.only`, `page.pause()` in committed code
- `if` / `try` / `catch` in test bodies unless unavoidable
- bypass existing `actions/ui/*` for behavior it already owns
- call `ui.*` actions or assertions in `*.test.ts` without a surrounding `test.step`
- duplicate magic-utterance smoke files — one focused spec per utterance pattern
- split one user journey into multiple `test()` cases when they repeat the same page load or expensive trigger — group in one case and use `test.step` in flows instead
- add a flow export used by only one test — inline the steps unless the journey is long enough to hurt readability (~30+ lines)

## Pitfalls

- **One inspect process** — still avoid duplicate `:5005` listeners.
- **File-by-file while developing** — faster than full suite; isolates server crashes.
- **Test timeout** — 1 minute in `playwright.config.ts` (`tests/mantle/` raise it with `test.describe.configure`, since LLM-driven skill activation needs more); long hangs are usually dead inspect, not slow assertions.
- **Barrel exports** — new `flows/*.flow.ts` → `flows/index.ts`; new `actions/ui/*.actions.ts` → `actions/ui/index.ts`. Missing exports cause unsafe-call lint on `flows.*`.
- **Pre-commit lints all of `e2e/`**, not staged files only. Keep WIP specs lint-clean or out of `tests/` until exports land.
- **`test.step` without `await`** — use `() => { expect(...) }`, not `async () => { ... }` when the callback has no `await` (`@typescript-eslint/require-await`).
- **Inspector `src/` changes** — rebuild `dist/` before commit or pre-commit `Inspector Build` fails.
- **REST vs inspect** — webhook smoke needs `rasa run --connector rest`, not `rasa inspect`.
- **Streamed welcome vs first bot bubble** — `utter_greeting` is LLM-rephrased and streams. Fixture readiness (`botMessageCountAtLeast(1)`) is true on the first streamed character, so a send in that window can drop the user message and hide the typing indicator until the greeting snapshot lands. `inspectorOptions.inspectMode` therefore also waits for **Agent turn ended**; in Preview specs, or after a manual `toggleInspectOn`, gate the first send yourself (`agentTurnEndedCountAtLeast`). Do not treat greeting-bubble text as a stable gate — wording is LLM-generated.
- **Turn boundaries, not mid-turn events** — `flows.chat` senders and `flows.mantle.activateSkillMode` wrap every send/quick-reply in `conversationLog.actions(page).completeTurn(...)`, which blocks until the next **Agent turn ended** (CALM and Mantle both emit it). Asserting only a mid-turn event (a slot set, a bot bubble) lets the next step race the rest of the turn: the canvas swaps to the next flow and remounts the view header, detaching menu items mid-click. Use `completeTurn` for any new sender, and expect bot-message counts to reflect the **whole** turn. Preview-mode specs cannot use it — conversation events only render in Inspect mode (`ConversationSession.tsx`), so they send via `ui.inspectorShell` directly.

## Where to put new code

- UI surface: `actions/ui/<feature>.actions.ts`
- Reusable multi-step journey: `flows/<feature>.flow.ts`
- Single-use steps for one spec: inline in `tests/<feature>.test.ts` with `test.step` + `ui.*`
- Fixture: `fixtures/<concern>-fixture.ts`
- Ops/setup: `README.md`
- Examples: `docs/authoring-tests.md`
